answer: Each identity claims a karst hollow, locks 70 credits, and files a pulse sounding each epoch, signed with its hollow key. Any peer may challenge by filing a rival pulse sounding for the same hollow; a karst auditor compares both against the hollow register, burns the wrong side's bond, pays half to the winner. Fees run 28+7(k-1): the 1000th costs 7021, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,524,500 plus 70,000 locked. Fees follow hollow order, not wallet, so splitting earns nothing. A rented-sounding ring fails: a borrowed sounding never matches the hollow key; an honest holder pays 28 and recovers the bond.
